title: What a retrieval miss can tell you
description: A note on separating candidate recall, ranking and answer grounding.
body: When a RAG answer is wrong, start by checking for the expected evidence in the candidate set. If it is absent, inspect ingestion, OCR, chunking and the retrieval query. If it is present but ranked poorly, compare the candidate list before and after reranking.

Questions that require several documents need their own slice. A single relevant result can look encouraging in a ranking metric while leaving the question unanswerable. Track full evidence coverage alongside the rank of the first relevant passage.
Then assess whether the answer uses the passages it retrieved. The next experiment should focus on the stage where evidence disappeared.

title: Where batch and CDC meet
description: Keeping the initial snapshot and the change stream aligned.
body: A batch load gives you a point-in-time view. Change data capture records what happened after a source position. The handover between those two views is where a pipeline can introduce gaps or duplicates.

Define record keys and replay behavior before wiring downstream transformations. Where append-only history matters, keep source offsets and operation metadata with the raw events. When current state is the goal, make updates idempotent.
The useful comparison is whether the same validation rules still pass after a restart, a repeated event or a schema change.
